audit.reasoning: All deciding quotations check out verbatim in held text (Gordon 2002:509 + fn. 9 in refs/; Hammond 1994 pp. 4-5 in the ROA PDF, now saved durably; H&R 1976 p. c.73 in held), and the sole primary 6σ attestation (wálakuwàntilu = 100100) plus Gordon's explicit schemata support the catalog string over StressTyp2's penult coding, so nothing in hand suggests the dominant-register coding is wrong. But the classification is second-hand twice over: a 2002 typological survey reading an unheld 1978 grammar, and a 1994 OT paper reading an unheld 1969 phonology article. The primary data (via Hammond) show free variation at 3σ, three lexical classes each at 4σ and 5σ with no stated default, and no words of 7-8σ, so lengths 5 and 7-8 rest entirely on Gordon's paraphrase of Hudson 1978. sources.citation: Hammond, Michael. 1994. An OT account of variability in Walmatjari stress. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-20. 14 pp.
sources.quote: From H&R 1969: disyllables initial; 'Trisyllabic words are stressed on either the first or second syllable'; quadrisyllables three lexical types (initial+penult secondary / fixed antepenult tjalánana / vacillating); five-syllable words three types (initial+penult wálakuwànti, initial+antepenult njántukùralu, vacillating); 'Only one six-syllabled word is cited and it has an initial main stress and antepenult secondary stress' (wálakuwàntilu).
sources.locator: pp. 4-5, exx. (7)-(11); p. 10 'the grammar provides no examples of seven-syllabled words'; fn. 11
